name: Interval Mod
description: You are given an array $$$a$$$ consisting of $$$n$$$ integers, as well as a parameter $$$k$$$ and an integer set $$$M=\{p, q\}$$$. You can perform the following operation on $$$a$$$ an arbitrary number of times (possibly zero): First, choose an interval $$$[l,r]$$$ ($$$1 \le l \le r \le n$$$) of length at least $$$k$$$ (i.e., $$$r-l+1\ge k$$$) and an integer $$$m \in M$$$; Then, set $$$a_i \gets a_i \bmod m$$$ for each $$$l \le i \le r$$$. You have to find the minimum possible value of $$$\sum \limits_{i=1}^n a_i$$$ after all operations.
input_specification: Each test contains multiple test cases. The first line contains the number of test cases $$$t$$$ ($$$1 \le t \le 10^4$$$). The description of the test cases follows. The first line of each test case contains four integers $$$n$$$, $$$k$$$, $$$p$$$, and $$$q$$$ ($$$1\le k\le n\le 10^5$$$, $$$1\le p \lt q\le 10^9$$$) — the length of $$$a$$$, the parameter, and the elements of $$$M$$$. The second line contains $$$n$$$ integers $$$a_1, a_2, \ldots, a_n$$$ ($$$1\le a_i\le 10^9$$$) — the elements of $$$a$$$. It is guaranteed that the sum of $$$n$$$ over all test cases does not exceed $$$10^5$$$.
output_specification: For each test case, output a single integer — the minimum possible value of $$$\sum \limits_{i=1}^n a_i$$$ after all operations.
subsubtopic: 461. Interval DP / Range DP / Matrix Chain Multiplication (MCM)
approach_summary: Iterate over interval length len from 1 to N and left endpoint l. Transition by splitting at midpoint k: dp[l][r] = min/max_k (dp[l][k] + dp[k+1][r] + cost) in O(N^3).

topic_editorial.summary: Interval / Range Dynamic Programming by interval length.
topic_editorial.key_invariant: The problem satisfies interval substructure: the optimal cost for range $[l, r]$ depends on splitting into subsegments $[l, k]$ and $[k+1, r]$ for some pivot $k \in [l, r-1]$. Computing shorter intervals first ensures that all subproblems are ready when evaluating longer intervals.
